lean.fidelity_note:
For nonzero perpendicular paths $k,\mathbf a\in\mathbb R^3$ satisfying $k\prime=-B^Tk$ and $\mathbf a\prime=-B\mathbf a+2(k\cdot B\mathbf a)k/|k|^2$ on a time set $J$, with $\operatorname{tr}B=0$, define $E_1=k/|k|$, $E_2=\mathbf a/|\mathbf a|$, $E_3=E_1\times E_2$, $B_{ij}=E_i\cdot BE_j$, and $\sigma=|k||\mathbf a|$. The formal statement gives an orthonormal frame and precisely the four identities $E_1'=-B_{12}E_2-B_{13}E_3$, $E_2'=B_{12}E_1-B_{32}E_3$, $E_3'=B_{13}E_1+B_{32}E_2$, and $(\log\sigma)'=B_{33}$. The three frame positions correspond in order to the paper’s subscripts $1,2,3$. Nonvanishing and perpendicularity are explicit hypotheses at every time in the set under consideration; a defined normalized triple alone would not guarantee orthonormality.

The paper assumes a smooth background $B$ on an interval. The formal statement does not require any time regularity of $B$ beyond the prescribed derivatives of $k$ and $\mathbf a$, and it permits relative derivatives on an arbitrary time set. On the paper’s interval these are the ordinary interior derivatives and the appropriate one-sided endpoint derivatives. No symmetry assumption on $B'+B^2$ appears. The stronger verdict refers to these weaker background and domain hypotheses with all four conclusions retained. It does not mean that the separate logarithmic derivatives of $|k|$ and $|\mathbf a|$, displayed inside the proof, are also conclusions of this declaration.
